method: Targeted primary-source checking plus publisher/Crossref/arXiv metadata. This is a narrative targeted search, not a systematic review. No citation was generated from memory without a matching fetched or inspected record. Reviewer 001's inspection levels are recorded separately from the author's metadata fetches; the review did not obtain the full Leinen et al. article.

entries.title: An empirical analysis of flaky tests
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd ACM SIGSOFT International Symposium on Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2014)
entries.inspection: Original paper, sections 2-4, checked by Reviewer 001 at https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs5154/2021sp/resources/LuoETAL14FlakyTestsAnalysis.pdf
entries.confirmed: Manual examination of 201 likely flaky-test-fixing commits from 51 Apache projects, including causes, fixes and failure manifestation.
entries.limit: Not a rerun-statistics study; do not describe its core design that way.

entries.title: An Empirical Study of Flaky Tests in Python
entries.venue: 2021 14th IEEE Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST)
entries.inspection: Full text sections II-III and abstract, checked by Reviewer 001 at https://arxiv.org/html/2101.09077v1
entries.confirmed: 22,352 projects and 876,186 tests; detection, tracing and manual classification; order-dependent 59% and infrastructure 28% shares.
entries.limit: More than repeated verdict collection; no categorical separation between controlled condition dependence and the wider flaky literature.

entries.title: The Effects of Computational Resources on Flaky Tests
entries.inspection: Author accepted manuscript, abstract and experiment setup/Phase I, checked by Reviewer 001 at https://www.jonbell.net/preprint/tse24-raft.pdf
entries.confirmed: 52 projects and 27 resource configurations; Phase I restricts individual resources as well as combinations, with repeated suite sessions.
entries.limit: Controlled single-factor experiments already exist; the terminal-key and recovery-procedure scope is the narrower difference.

entries.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Environmental Flakiness in JavaScript Tests
entries.inspection: Full text sections III, IV, VI and VIII, checked by Reviewer 001 at https://arxiv.org/html/2602.19098v1
entries.confirmed: Varies OS, Node.js and browsers; manually inspects failures; proposes a mitigation that skips or reports environment-dependent tests. Its categories include repeatable compatibility failures.
entries.limit: Contrast measured factors and endpoints, not an asserted absence of condition-dependent flakiness research.

entries.title: A Survey of Flaky Tests
entries.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)
entries.inspection: Author PDF sections 1, 3 and 5 plus bibliography, checked by Reviewer 001 at https://o-parry.github.io/papers/2021a.pdf and https://www.gregorykapfhammer.com/research/papers/parry2022/
entries.confirmed: 76 papers; environmental and implementation dependence within a broad conception of flakiness; reviews targeted perturbation tools.
entries.limit: A missing terminal keyword is not proof of an unstudied category. Cite TOSEM 31(1), Article 17 (2022); the author PDF is dated October 2021.

entries.title: An Empirical Study of Detected and Undetected Flaky Test Failures in Real-World CI Pipelines
entries.inspection: Author institution metadata, abstract and replication README checked by Reviewer 001; full article not obtained.
entries.confirmed: 8.8 billion executions from four projects; apparently deterministic failures validated with reruns in fresh original CI environments.
entries.limit: Do not reduce this study to passive CI-history mining. Because the full article was not obtained, no claim is made that it lacks a specific method.

entries.title: Software Quality Journal
entries.scope_summary: Academic and practical knowledge about creating, using and maintaining software systems; quality management, methods, tools and products, including software testing, quality measurement and case studies.
entries.scope_caveat: The scope includes case studies; this does not mean the submission system offers a separate Case Study article type, and it is not a fit or acceptance guarantee.
entries.ccf_rank_claim: CCF C according to third-party indexes; the full official CCF classification page was not obtained, so the rank remains to be verified against the official catalogue.
entries.review_role_note: Reviewer 001 is the AI review role used in this conversation, not an independent human referee or journal reviewer. Actual AI method/analysis use should be disclosed under the journal policy.

limitations: The CCF rank is not certified here; verify against the official CCF catalogue before submission.
Article types and formatting requirements must be read from the current submission guidelines at submission time.
The literature search is a targeted narrative search, not a systematic review; absence of a dedicated terminal-environment study is a search observation, not a proof of novelty.
Reviewer 001 did not obtain the full Leinen et al. article; no method-absence claim about that study is certified.
Bibliographic metadata does not establish the semantic correctness of any comparison; the comparison sentences are author arguments bounded by the recorded primary-source checks.
